A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same learning-speed and catastrophic-forgetting study, despite the changed title and method name. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the work.

before.justification: V1 reports original neural-network experiments measuring forgetting, replay-buffer composition and classification accuracy, including repeated-run results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds robustness sweeps, scoring-function comparisons, fixed-parameter sampling results and further class-incremental analyses.

M1.justification: Goldilocks is renamed Speed-Based Sampling (SBS). Equation 1 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure: average epoch-wise correctness, remove the quickest and slowest fractions, and sample uniformly from the remainder. SBS-fix assigns constants to existing parameters rather than introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, including task-incremental and class-incremental classification, rotation classification and random-label scenarios. CIFAR-100-20 introduces a finer partition of existing classes; this changes the evaluation protocol rather than the represented dataset or task domain.

E2.justification: V2 adds LARS to the replay-sampling comparisons, including the retained two-task experiments in Table 3. Random sampling, maximum entropy, IPM, GSS and Herding remain. Figure 25 additionally compares learning speed with uncertainty, final loss and c-score as example-scoring functions.

E3.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-100-20 partitions, 5k-buffer multi-task sweeps, and controlled variations in optimizers, architectures, training epochs, learning rates, regularization and class splits. Reported settings also change: Figure 4c specifies a 20k TinyImageNet buffer instead of v1's 10k, although v2 Figure 22c inconsistently says 1k. These are documented protocol additions and revisions, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing dataset, architecture and subsequent-task analyses, v2 adds systematic training-setting sensitivity tests (Appendix D), fixed-versus-tuned sampling, alternative scoring functions (Appendix G), and multi-task forgetting/composition analyses. Class-incremental forgetting dynamics receive additional direct analysis. V1's separate class-incremental GEM composition grid is no longer presented.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten-network/repetition means and standard-error reporting, without an explicit increase in runs or new inferential procedures. However, v1 Figure 16's separate GEM heatmap standard errors are omitted while the corresponding mean-results analysis remains in v2 Figure 14c. Changed error magnitudes alone do not establish a new estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for sampling comparisons, class-incremental evaluation, robustness sweeps and alternative scores. For the retained CIFAR-100-2/1k comparison, Goldilocks/SBS changes from 71.53 ± 7.31 in v1 Table 2 to 71.71 with standard error 0.22 in v2 Tables 3–4. Section 2.4 also corrects the buffer-size correlation from +0.966 to -0.966. Results under newly introduced settings are additional evidence, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The continual-learning setup, learning-speed definition in Equation 1, classification matrix and remembered-example definition remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the expanded behavioral explanations and empirical score comparisons do not introduce new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that faster-learned examples resist forgetting, stronger memory capacity extends retention toward slower-learned examples, and speed-based replay selection improves diverse continual-learning methods. V2 emphasizes behavioral observation and reorganizes the contributions, but retains the central scientific claims and state-of-the-art performance claim.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies v1's broadly shared buffer preferences by explaining that class-incremental learning slightly favors faster-learned examples because task inference is harder. It adds that short training schedules remain useful when the network converges, despite noisier speed estimates, and explains the preference for learning speed over alternative scores. The single-epoch streaming limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 50 epochs per task for the multi-method comparison, baseline random/reservoir buffer handling, a q = s = 20% default, and optimizer-specific settings for the added sensitivity experiments. RotNet tuning and runtime guidance are expanded. The existing ResNet-18, SGD and TITAN X configuration is largely relocated to Appendix A.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds distinctions from curriculum and self-paced learning and connections to active, semi-supervised and transfer learning, with corresponding citations. Appendix G introduces the uncertainty-score and c-score references. The central positioning as a data-centric study of forgetting and a general replay-sampling strategy remains.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, renames Goldilocks to SBS, and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and contribution list. Buffer-composition observations move into Section 2, while Section 3 separately develops SBS, its evaluation and limitations. The appendices are reorganized and explanations of tuning and practical use are expanded.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to two columns. Classification matrices receive new colors and ordering, and composition heatmaps display accuracy differences from uniform sampling instead of absolute accuracy. Benchmark plots are consolidated, tables are expanded and reorganized, and numerous new analysis panels are added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for v1's broad robustness claims through controlled sensitivity tests, fuller class-incremental analyses, alternative-score comparisons and fixed-versus-tuned sampling results. These address dependence on training choices, the scoring proxy and parameter tuning, while the reorganized presentation improves usability. Conflicting buffer-size captions and unexplained standard-error revisions remain, but the added evidence provides a substantial overall improvement.
